ESA Family FAQ

Can I use ESA funds to buy a laptop?

Short answer: it depends entirely on your state's program. Some allow it outright, some only after tuition is paid, and a few exclude it completely. Here's the real rule in each of our service states.

All Inclusive Tutoring Solutions · ESA vendor

🧩 The pattern across most states

ESA programs almost always treat "educational technology" as its own spending category — separate from tuition, curriculum, and therapy — and they attach one or more of these guardrails:

  • Frequency limits — often once every 2–3 years per device, not annually.
  • Price caps — a maximum dollar amount per device (commonly $1,000–$1,500).
  • Purpose restrictions — the device must be primarily educational, not general family use.
  • Marketplace-only purchases — bought through ClassWallet or Odyssey, not reimbursed after the fact.

Always confirm through the family's official program portal before purchasing — rules get updated year to year.

Allowed Allowed with limits Not allowed
Arizona
✅ Allowed
Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) · ClassWallet

Personal computers, laptops, and tablets are explicitly listed as allowable purchases in the ESA Parent Handbook. Entertainment devices (TVs, phones, game consoles) are excluded.

Florida
🚫 Not allowed (PEP)
Personalized Education Program (PEP) · Step Up For Students

Under Florida law, PEP students cannot use scholarship funds to purchase laptops, computers, or other digital devices. This has been a point of active parent advocacy — families have petitioned to change it, but as of now it remains excluded. (Florida's separate FES-UA program for students with disabilities does allow technology purchases — different program, different rules.)

Louisiana
⚠️ Allowed, capped
LA GATOR Scholarship Program · Odyssey

Laptops are an eligible marketplace purchase, but families may buy only one such device every 3 years. Buy a laptop this year, and you can't purchase another device in that category again for three years (though a different type of device is fine sooner).

Indiana
🚫 Not allowed
Indiana Education Scholarship Account (INESA)

Personal computers, laptops, and other technological devices are explicitly on Indiana's excluded expense list — under both the tuition/fee category and the curricular materials category. Educational software and apps are fine; the hardware itself is not.

Iowa
⚠️ Allowed, with a catch
Students First Act ESA · Odyssey

Laptops, desktops, and tablets are eligible — but only after tuition and fees are paid in full for the semester, using whatever balance remains. Also note: Iowa's ESA requires enrollment in an accredited private school — homeschoolers don't qualify for this particular program.

Montana
⚠️ Allowed, program status uncertain
Special Needs Equal Opportunity ESA · Office of Public Instruction

Educational technology and materials are reimbursable expenses for this special-needs-only ESA. Important: the program is currently in active litigation. A court stay allows currently enrolled students to keep receiving reimbursements through June 30, 2026, but the program's future beyond that is undecided. Worth flagging to Montana families directly.

New Hampshire
⚠️ Allowed, with paperwork
Education Freedom Account (EFA) · Children's Scholarship Fund NH

Laptops and desktops are allowed ("computer device" is a defined category), but families must submit a Computer Device Build Form and are encouraged to buy a warranty — components that fail without warranty coverage aren't replaceable with EFA funds. Tablets are capped at $1,500 per item.

North Carolina
✅ Allowed
ESA+ · ClassWallet

Desktop and laptop computers, tablets, and interactive whiteboards are listed under "Computers and Related" educational technology. Accessories (keyboard, mouse, case, printer) are allowed once every 3 years per device. Note: ESA+ specifically serves students with disabilities.

South Carolina
✅ Allowed
Education Scholarship Trust Fund (ESTF) · ClassWallet

"Computer hardware or other technological devices" is a named qualifying expense category under state law. Purchases go through the ClassWallet marketplace.

Utah
⚠️ Allowed, capped
Utah Fits All Scholarship · Odyssey

Laptops, desktops, and tablets are eligible, but a computer or tech device can only be purchased once every 3 years per student, and price caps apply (tablets are capped at $1,500). A 2026 state audit flagged overspending on high-end laptops, so expect scrutiny on pricier models.

West Virginia
⚠️ Allowed, capped
Hope Scholarship

Computers, printers, and required software are eligible under the "Technology" category, with a 2-year repurchase restriction per device category. A laptop bought this February can't be replaced with Hope funds until two Februaries from now.

Wyoming
✅ Allowed
Steamboat Legacy Scholarship ESA

"Technology, such as computers and educational software" is listed among approved expense categories. Note: the program is currently the subject of an ongoing legal challenge, though it's operating normally at present following the Wyoming Supreme Court lifting an earlier injunction.
